problems: "This also fixed" is a bit clunky; the integrate fix could arguably go under integrals.
Names the private helper `_solve_system`, an implementation detail users don't call directly; the user-facing function is `solve`.
"Transcendental bases" is wrong: the bases in the fixed case are 2 and 3, which are integers. The transcendental terms are the log(2) and log(3) that come up during integration.
Overgeneralizes to all products of exponentials and is vague ("crash"), so users can't tell which inputs are affected.

structured_output.rationale: The PR adds an early return to `_solve_system` when there are no symbols to solve for. Previously, systems of constant transcendental terms like `log(2) + log(3)` raised an IndexError, and this made `integrate(2**(2+3*x)*3**(5+7*x), x)` fail. Candidate A describes this accurately in terms of the public `solve` function and gives the exact integral that now works. Candidate B names the private `_solve_system` helper, and its integrals bullet calls the bases "transcendental" when they are integers. It also describes the fix too broadly, as covering all products of exponentials.
